1.5 Trigonometry

Identities · equations · exact values · graphs and transformations

CIE 9709 Paper 1 Pure Mathematics 1, syllabus 1.5.
重要本节考纲要求

本页依据 9709 Mathematics 2026–2027 syllabus 1.5 Trigonometry：

  • sketch and use sine、cosine、tangent graphs，角度可用 degrees 或 radians；
  • 使用 30^\circ、45^\circ、60^\circ 及相关角的 exact values；
  • 使用 \sin^{-1}x、\cos^{-1}x、\tan^{-1}x 的 principal values；
  • 使用基本 trigonometric identities，解给定 interval 内的 equations；
  • 识别 y=a\sin(bx)+c、y=a\cos(bx)+c 的 amplitude、period、midline 与 transformations。

下列 16 组题目均来自工作区保存的 Paper 1 原始 past-paper PDF。题干只把 PDF 排版符号整理为 LaTeX，没有改写或编造题目；答案按对应 mark scheme 的得分步骤展开。

1. Core knowledge

Exact values and identities

\sin\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac12,\quad\cos\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac12,\quad\sin\frac{\pi}{4}=\cos\frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{\sqrt2}{2},\quad\sin\frac{\pi}{3}=\cos\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.

\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1,\qquad\tan x=\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}.

做 identity proof 时先统一分母，再使用 \sin^2x+\cos^2x=1；解 equation 时最后必须按题目 interval 补齐所有 quadrant solutions。

Equations and graphs

若 0\le x\le2\pi，则

\sin x=a\Rightarrow x=\alpha,\pi-\alpha;\quad\cos x=a\Rightarrow x=\alpha,2\pi-\alpha;\quad\tan x=a\Rightarrow x=\alpha,\pi+\alpha.

对 y=a\sin(bx)+c 或 y=a\cos(bx)+c：

\text{amplitude}=|a|,\qquad\text{period}=\frac{2\pi}{|b|},\qquad\text{midline }y=c.

Ratios, exact values and identities

在 right triangle 中

\sin\theta=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}},\qquad \cos\theta=\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}},\qquad \tan\theta=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}.

除 30^\circ、45^\circ、60^\circ 外，要熟悉相关的 negative-angle、supplementary-angle 和 quadrant signs。基本恒等式为

\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1,

并可由此得到 1+\tan^2\theta=\sec^2\theta（在使用 sec notation 的题目中）。证明 identity 时通常先把所有 terms 写成 \sin、\cos，再统一分母或使用 \sin^2+\cos^2=1。

Solving trigonometric equations

先 isolate 一个 trig ratio，再求 principal angle。对 0\le\theta\le2\pi：

\sin\theta=a\Rightarrow\theta=\alpha,\pi-\alpha;\quad \cos\theta=a\Rightarrow\theta=\alpha,2\pi-\alpha;\quad \tan\theta=a\Rightarrow\theta=\alpha,\pi+\alpha.

若方程含有 \sin^2\theta、\cos^2\theta 或同时含 \sin\theta,\cos\theta，可先用 identity 或乘以 \sin\theta / \cos\theta 化成 quadratic；factorise 后必须检查每个 root 是否在 [-1,1] 以及是否满足原方程的 denominator restrictions。

Graph features and inverse trig

对 y=a\sin(bx)+c、y=a\cos(bx)+c，|a| 是 amplitude，2\pi/|b| 是 period，y=c 是 midline；a<0 会产生 reflection in the x-axis。Tangent graph 的 period 是 \pi，并有 vertical asymptotes。

\sin^{-1}、\cos^{-1}、\tan^{-1} 表示 inverse functions 的 principal values，不是 reciprocal。最后答案必须统一成题目要求的 degrees 或 radians，并列出指定 interval 内的全部 solutions。

2. Verified Paper 1 past-paper questions

Question 1 · 9709/11/M/J/20 Q7(a–b)

  1. Prove \frac{1+\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}+\frac{\cos\theta}{1+\sin\theta}=\frac2{\cos\theta}.

  2. Hence solve the equation when the right-hand side is 3/\sin\theta, for 0\le\theta\le2\pi. [3+3]

Show detailed mark scheme answer

\frac{(1+\sin\theta)^2+\cos^2\theta}{\cos\theta(1+\sin\theta)}=\frac{2+2\sin\theta}{\cos\theta(1+\sin\theta)}=\boxed{\frac2{\cos\theta}}.

Then 2/\cos\theta=3/\sin\theta, so \tan\theta=3/2. Therefore

\boxed{\theta=\tan^{-1}\frac32,\ \pi+\tan^{-1}\frac32=0.983,\ 4.12\text{ rad}}.
Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-11.pdf, Q7(a–b), and matching 9709-s20-ms-11.pdf.

Question 2 · 9709/12/M/J/20 Q2(a–b)

Express 3\cos\theta=8\tan\theta as a quadratic in \sin\theta. Hence find the acute angle in degrees. [3+2]

Show detailed mark scheme answer

Multiplying by \cos\theta and using \cos^2\theta=1-\sin^2\theta:

3(1-\sin^2\theta)=8\sin\theta\Longrightarrow\boxed{3\sin^2\theta+8\sin\theta-3=0}.

Thus (3\sin\theta-1)(\sin\theta+3)=0. Only \sin\theta=1/3 is possible, so

\boxed{\theta=\sin^{-1}\frac13=19.5^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.
Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-12.pdf, Q2(a–b), and matching 9709-s20-ms-12.pdf.

Question 3 · 9709/12/M/J/20 Q9(a–c)

f(x)=2-3\sin2x,\qquad g(x)=-2f(x),\qquad0\le x\le\pi.

State the ranges of f and g. [3]

  1. Sketch, on the given diagram, the graph of y=g(x).

  2. Describe fully a sequence of transformations that maps the curve y=f(x) on to y=h(x), where

h(x)=g(x+\pi),\qquad -\pi\le x\le0.

[2+3]

Show detailed mark scheme answer

Because 2x covers a complete cycle, -1\le\sin2x\le1. Hence

\boxed{-1\le f(x)\le5}.

Multiplying the range by -2 reverses the endpoints:

\boxed{-10\le g(x)\le2}.

  1. Since g=-2f, the graph has the same x-coordinates as f, with all y-coordinates multiplied by -2. It passes through (0,-4), (\pi/4,2), (3\pi/4,-10) and (\pi,-4).

  2. Since f(x+\pi)=f(x),

h(x)=-2f(x+\pi).

Thus translate the graph \pi units to the left, reflect it in the x-axis, and stretch it parallel to the y-axis by scale factor 2.
Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-12.pdf, Q9(a–c), and matching 9709-s20-ms-12.pdf.

Question 4 · 9709/11/O/N/20 Q7(a–b)

  1. Show \frac{\sin\theta}{1-\sin\theta}-\frac{\sin\theta}{1+\sin\theta}=2\tan^2\theta.

  2. Hence solve the equation when the left-hand side is 8, for 0<\theta<\pi. [3+3]

Show detailed mark scheme answer

\frac{2\sin^2\theta}{1-\sin^2\theta}=\frac{2\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta}=\boxed{2\tan^2\theta}.

So 2\tan^2\theta=8, giving \tan\theta=\pm2. The two solutions in (0,\pi) are

\boxed{\theta=\tan^{-1}2,\ \pi-\tan^{-1}2=1.107,\ 2.034\text{ rad}}.
Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709_w20_qp_11.pdf, Q7(a–b), and matching 9709_w20_ms_11.pdf.

Question 5 · 9709/13/M/J/21 Q4(a–b)

Show \frac{\tan x+\sin x}{\tan x-\sin x}=k may be expressed as \frac{1+\cos x}{1-\cos x}=k. Hence express \cos x in terms of k. [2+2]

Show detailed mark scheme answer

Using \tan x=\sin x/\cos x,

\frac{\tan x+\sin x}{\tan x-\sin x}=\frac{\sin x(1+\cos x)}{\sin x(1-\cos x)}=\boxed{\frac{1+\cos x}{1-\cos x}}.

Rearrange:

1+\cos x=k(1-\cos x)\Longrightarrow\boxed{\cos x=\frac{k-1}{k+1}}.
Source: PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_s21_qp_13.pdf, Q4(a–b), and matching 9709_s21_ms_13.pdf.

Question 6 · 9709/11/O/N/21 Q3

Solve by factorising:

6\cos\theta\tan\theta-3\cos\theta+4\tan\theta-2=0,\qquad0^\circ\le\theta\le180^\circ.

Show detailed mark scheme answer

3\cos\theta(2\tan\theta-1)+2(2\tan\theta-1)=0,

so (2\tan\theta-1)(3\cos\theta+2)=0. Therefore \tan\theta=1/2 or \cos\theta=-2/3:

\boxed{\theta=26.6^\circ\text{ or }131.8^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.
Source: PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_w21_qp_11.pdf, Q3, and matching 9709_w21_ms_11.pdf.

Question 7 · 9709/12/O/N/21 Q1

Solve 2\cos\theta=7-\frac3{\cos\theta} for -90^\circ<\theta<90^\circ. [4]

Show detailed mark scheme answer

Multiplying by \cos\theta:

2\cos^2\theta-7\cos\theta+3=0=(2\cos\theta-1)(\cos\theta-3).

The root \cos\theta=3 is impossible. Thus \cos\theta=1/2, and the symmetric interval gives

\boxed{\theta=-60^\circ\text{ or }60^\circ}.
Source: PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_w21_qp_12.pdf, Q1, and matching 9709_w21_ms_12.pdf.

Question 8 · 9709/13/O/N/21 Q7(a–b)

Show that \frac{\tan x+\cos x}{\tan x-\cos x}=k becomes (k+1)\sin^2x+(k-1)\sin x-(k+1)=0. Hence solve the original equation for k=4, 0^\circ\le x\le360^\circ. [4+4]

Show detailed mark scheme answer

Multiplying by \cos x and using \cos^2x=1-\sin^2x gives

\boxed{(k+1)\sin^2x+(k-1)\sin x-(k+1)=0}.

For k=4:

5\sin^2x+3\sin x-5=0,\qquad\sin x=\frac{-3\pm\sqrt{109}}{10}.

Only the positive root is admissible, so

\boxed{x=48.1^\circ\text{ or }131.9^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.
Source: PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_w21_qp_13.pdf, Q7(a–b), and matching 9709_w21_ms_13.pdf.

Question 9 · 9709/12/M/J/23 Q1

Solve 4\sin\theta+\tan\theta=0 for 0^\circ<\theta<180^\circ. [3]

Show detailed mark scheme answer

\sin\theta\left(4+\frac1{\cos\theta}\right)=0.

The endpoints are excluded, so \sin\theta\ne0. Therefore \cos\theta=-1/4, and the second-quadrant solution is

\boxed{\theta=\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac14\right)=104.5^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.
Source: PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_s23_qp_12.pdf, Q1, and matching 9709_s23_ms_12.pdf.

Question 10 · 9709/12/M/J/23 Q7(a)(i–ii)

  1. By expanding (\cos\theta+\sin\theta)^2, find the three solutions of (\cos\theta+\sin\theta)^2=1 for 0\le\theta\le\pi.

  2. Hence verify that the only solutions of \cos\theta+\sin\theta=1 are 0 and \frac12\pi. [3+2]

Show detailed mark scheme answer

(\cos\theta+\sin\theta)^2=1+\sin2\theta.

Thus \sin2\theta=0, giving

\boxed{\theta=0,\frac{\pi}{2},\pi}.

Substitution into the unsquared equation gives 1,1,-1 respectively, so

\boxed{\theta=0\text{ and }\frac{\pi}{2}}.
Source: PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_s23_qp_12.pdf, Q7(a)(i–ii), and matching 9709_s23_ms_12.pdf.

Question 11 · 9709/12/O/N/23 Q5(a–b)

The first, second and third terms of a geometric progression are \sin\theta, \cos\theta and 2-\sin\theta, where \theta radians is acute. Find \theta. [3]

  1. Using this value of \theta, find the sum of the first 10 terms of the progression. Give the answer in the form \dfrac{b}{\sqrt{c}-1}, where b and c are integers to be found. [3]
Show detailed mark scheme answer

The GP condition is \cos^2\theta=\sin\theta(2-\sin\theta). Since \cos^2\theta=1-\sin^2\theta,

1-\sin^2\theta=2\sin\theta-\sin^2\theta\Longrightarrow\sin\theta=\frac12.

Acuteness selects

\boxed{\theta=\frac{\pi}{6}}.

  1. The common ratio is

r=\frac{\cos(\pi/6)}{\sin(\pi/6)}=\sqrt3.

Therefore

S_{10}=\frac{\frac12\left((\sqrt3)^{10}-1\right)}{\sqrt3-1} =\boxed{\frac{121}{\sqrt3-1}}, so b=121 and c=3.
Source: PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_w23_qp_12.pdf, Q5(a–b), and matching 9709_w23_ms_12.pdf.

Question 12 · 9709/12/M/J/24 Q5(a–b)

  1. Prove \frac{\sin^2x-\cos x-1}{1+\cos x}=-\cos x.

  2. Hence solve \frac{\sin^2x-\cos x-1}{2+2\cos x}=\frac14 for 0^\circ\le x\le360^\circ. [3+3]

Show detailed mark scheme answer

\sin^2x-\cos x-1=1-\cos^2x-\cos x-1=-\cos x(1+\cos x),

which proves (a). In (b), the denominator is doubled, so the left side is -\frac12\cos x. Hence \cos x=-1/2 and

\boxed{x=120^\circ\text{ or }240^\circ}.
Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p12.pdf, Q5(a–b), and matching ms-202406-mathematics-p12.pdf.

Question 13 · 9709/12/M/J/24 Q3(a–b)

  1. Show that \frac{7\tan\theta}{\cos\theta}+12=0 becomes 12\sin^2\theta-7\sin\theta-12=0.

  2. Hence solve the original equation for 0^\circ\le\theta\le360^\circ. [3+3]

Show detailed mark scheme answer

Multiplying by \cos^2\theta gives 7\sin\theta+12\cos^2\theta=0. Replacing \cos^2\theta by 1-\sin^2\theta gives

\boxed{12\sin^2\theta-7\sin\theta-12=0}.

The factors are (3\sin\theta+4)(4\sin\theta-3), so \sin\theta=3/4. Therefore

\boxed{\theta=48.6^\circ\text{ or }131.4^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.
Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p12.pdf, Q3(a–b), and matching ms-202406-mathematics-p12.pdf.

Question 14 · 9709/13/M/J/24 Q4(a–b)

  1. Show that \cos x(7\tan x-5\cos x)=1 can be written as a\sin^2x+b\sin x+c=0.

  2. Hence solve it for 0^\circ<x<180^\circ. [3+3]

Show detailed mark scheme answer

7\sin x-5\cos^2x=1\Longrightarrow7\sin x-5(1-\sin^2x)=1,

so

5\sin^2x+7\sin x-6=0=(5\sin x-3)(\sin x+2).

Only \sin x=3/5 is valid. Hence

\boxed{x=\sin^{-1}\frac35=36.9^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.
Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p13.pdf, Q4(a–b), and matching ms-202406-mathematics-p13.pdf.

Question 15 · 9709/11/O/N/24 Q8(a–b)

  1. \beta is between 90^\circ and 180^\circ and \sin\beta=a. Express \tan^2\beta-3\sin\beta\cos\beta in terms of a.

  2. Solve \sin^2\theta+2\cos^2\theta=4\sin\theta+3 for 0^\circ<\theta<360^\circ. [3+5]

Show detailed mark scheme answer

In quadrant II, \cos\beta=-\sqrt{1-a^2}. Thus

\boxed{\tan^2\beta-3\sin\beta\cos\beta=\frac{a^2}{1-a^2}+3a\sqrt{1-a^2}}.

For (b), use \cos^2\theta=1-\sin^2\theta:

\sin^2\theta+2(1-\sin^2\theta)=4\sin\theta+3\Longrightarrow\sin^2\theta+4\sin\theta+1=0.

The valid root is \sin\theta=-2+\sqrt3, giving

\boxed{\theta=195.6^\circ\text{ or }344.4^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.
Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202410-mathematics-p11.pdf, Q8(a–b), and matching ms-202410-mathematics-p11.pdf.

Question 16 · 9709/13/O/N/24 Q4

Solve 4\sin^4\theta+12\sin^2\theta-7=0 for 0^\circ\le\theta\le360^\circ. [4]

Show detailed mark scheme answer

Let u=\sin^2\theta. Then 4u^2+12u-7=0, so

u=\frac{-12\pm16}{8}=1/2\text{ or }-3.

Reject u=-3. Hence \sin^2\theta=1/2, and

\boxed{\theta=45^\circ,\ 135^\circ,\ 225^\circ,\ 315^\circ}.
Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202410-mathematics-p13.pdf, Q4, and matching ms-202410-mathematics-p13.pdf.
